description: Default benign-context rules. They NEVER suppress findings: every entry below uses downgrades only (severity drops one step, score halves, the finding stays visible). Rationale: class and permission context is spoofable — a malicious app can embed a password-manager package name or declare a device-admin permission — so a full hide would let malware silence its own detections. A downgrade keeps the signal while cutting the false-positive noise from legitimate apps.

rules.name: Password manager autofill (accessibility + overlay by design)
rules.description: Password managers drive overlay windows and accessibility APIs for OS-level autofill. Their a11y API footprint overlaps the banking-overlay patterns.
rules.reason: Password managers legitimately combine accessibility services with overlay windows for autofill; their API footprint matches the a11y-overlay banking patterns. Package-name context is spoofable, so findings are downgraded (kept visible), never suppressed.

rules.name: Device-admin / MDM agent (management APIs by design)
rules.description: Enterprise MDM agents hold BIND_DEVICE_ADMIN and legitimately use accessibility, overlay and network APIs for device management.
rules.reason: MDM agents are device administrators by design and combine overlay, accessibility and INTERNET for management. Permission context is declarable by any app, so findings are downgraded (kept visible), never suppressed.
